history.dynasty: Eastern Ganga dynasty (King Langula Narasingha Deva)
history.summary: The Khirachora Gopinatha Temple at Remuna is one of Odisha's most beloved Vaishnava pilgrimage centres, dedicated to Krishna as Gopinatha. Legend holds the black-stone image was carved by Sri Rama's arrow at Chitrakuta and worshipped by Sita; Eastern Ganga King Langula Narasingha Deva brought it to Remuna in the 13th century (the Kendupatana copper plate shows Narasimha Deva-II granting from his royal camp at Remuna in 1295 AD) and had the two great tanks Bajra (Brajapokhari) and Kuta Pokhari dug. The name 'Khirachora' (milk-thief) comes from the pastime in which the Lord hid a pot of his famous khira (Amrita-Keli, a preparation of condensed milk, sugar, cream and raisins) under his cloth for his devotee Madhavendra Puri, who had stopped at Remuna en route to Puri and longed to taste it. Remuna is also called Gupt Vrindavana; Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu visited on his way from Katwa to Puri and narrated the khira pastime to his followers. CSV town correction: the temple is NOT in Balasore town - it stands at Remuna, about 9 km from Balasore (sources disagree whether east or west of Balasore - verify direction locally). Remuna's name is said to come from 'Ramaniya' (very good-looking). The deities Govinda and Madana Mohana were brought from Vrindavan around 1938 by devotee Chaitanya Dasa Babaji (per Odisha endowments).

name: Khirachora Gopinatha Temple
town: Remuna (CSV town 'Balasore' is the district HQ city; the temple is at Remuna, ~9 km away)
town_description: Remuna is a small town in Balasore district, Odisha, about 9 km from Balasore city, roughly halfway between Howrah and Bhubaneswar. Called Gupt Vrindavana in Vaishnava tradition, it is known almost entirely for the Khirachora Gopinatha Temple and its tanks.
tradition: Vaishnavism (Krishna worship; closely associated with Gaudiya Vaishnavism and Chaitanya Mahaprabhu)

travel.airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar (~200 km - verify); Kolkata airport (~250 km) is another option.
travel.railway: Balasore railway station (Balasore Junction) on the Howrah-Chennai line, about 9 km away.
travel.road: Auto-rickshaws from Balasore bus stand, Remuna Golei, or the railway station; the Emami Jagannath Temple and Gaudiya Matha are nearby stops on the way.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather; the famous khira prasad (Amrita-Keli) is available year-round.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Typical Vaishnavite temple darshan hours (verify - no authoritative schedule found online; confirm locally).
